svg.title: Fast leader handover: messages and state changes
svg.desc: Leader B starts block 104 on expected parent 103. Its Pool derives ParentReady locally. Happy handover keeps the work. Sad handover uses UpdateParent to reset execution.

g.aria-label: Leader A. Show explanation
g.title: The outgoing leader produces slots 100 to 103. Its last block is the expected parent for the incoming leader’s first block.

g.aria-label: Leader B: Replay and block producer. Show explanation
g.title: These processes run inside Leader B. They execute the parent and produce slots 104 to 107. They can start work on an expected parent before its certificate arrives.

g.aria-label: Leader B: Vote and certificate Pool. Show explanation
g.title: This process also runs inside Leader B. It verifies votes and certificates. It derives ParentReady locally and sends the selected ready parent to block production.

g.aria-label: Other validators. Show explanation
g.title: The other validators receive block data, execute blocks, and exchange votes and certificates. Each validator checks its own parent and vote conditions before it sends an initial notar vote.

text.tspan: Happy handover: ready parent is block 103
Sad handover: ready parent is a different block Q

g.aria-label: M01: Block 103 data. Show explanation
g.title: Leader A sends its last block through the normal data-distribution path. Leader B needs that block’s data and state before it can use it as the expected parent.

g.aria-label: M02: Block 103 data. Show explanation
g.title: Other validators receive the same proposed parent block. They execute it and can send the votes that establish parent support.

g.aria-label: M03: Execute 103; use it as expected parent. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B executes block 103 and starts from its state. The early-start path saves certificate-wait time when this expected parent later becomes ready.

g.aria-label: M04: BlockHeader for 104, parent 103. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B announces the initial parent in block 104’s header. Receiving validators can identify the history and state that the early block data extends.

g.aria-label: M05: Early transaction data for 104. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B streams transaction data while parent evidence is still in transit. This uses time that would otherwise be spent waiting for ParentReady.

g.aria-label: M06: Parent votes or valid certificates. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B receives parent votes or certificates from other validators. It can build a certificate or verify a received certificate. It does not need every individual vote if a valid certificate arrives.

g.aria-label: M07: Check parent and intervening skip certificates. Show explanation
g.title: Pool checks the selected parent’s certificate and each required skip certificate. These checks establish whether the new leader window can extend that parent.

g.aria-label: M08: Local ready-parent notification. Show explanation
g.title: Pool derives ParentReady. Agave sends the selected parent to block production through an internal ProduceWindow event. This communication stays inside Leader B. Leader A does not send permission to begin the window.

g.aria-label: M09: Keep the early work. Show explanation
g.title: The ready parent is the same block as the expected parent. Leader B can keep its provisional execution work. No UpdateParent marker is necessary.

g.aria-label: M10: Stop old record input. Show explanation
g.title: The ready parent differs from the expected parent. Leader B stops and drains the old record input. Old execution records must not enter the new parent’s execution sequence.

g.aria-label: M11: UpdateParent naming Q. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B puts the new parent’s slot and block ID into an UpdateParent marker. Other validators need the same execution restart point. This marker is part of the block stream.

g.aria-label: M12: Rebuild execution on Q. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B recreates its execution state from Q and reschedules accumulated transactions. The completed block must describe execution on the ready parent.

g.aria-label: M13: Discard old execution effects; use Q. Show explanation
g.title: Receiving validators discard execution effects before UpdateParent and continue from Q. All validators must use the same parent state. The earlier transmitted data remains part of the block data.

g.aria-label: M14: Remaining block 104 data and footer. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B finishes the first block after it has resolved its parent. The completed block lets receivers finish execution and check their voting conditions.

text.tspan: M14: Remaining block 104 data and footer

g.aria-label: M15: Complete execution; check own voting conditions. Show explanation
g.title: Each receiver completes block execution and checks the parent condition and its own first-vote state. Receiving a block or an UpdateParent marker alone does not authorize a notar vote.

g.aria-label: M16: Ordinary notar votes for completed block 104. Show explanation
g.title: Eligible validators send initial notar votes for the completed block. These are ordinary Alpenglow votes. Fast leader handover does not add a special consensus vote type.

g.aria-label: M17: Produce subsequent blocks 105 to 107. Show explanation
g.title: Leader B continues its window. Each later block extends the preceding block. Later block production can overlap with votes for block 104. B does not wait for a certificate for 104 before it produces 105.

text.tspan: Dashed arrow: internal notification. Self arrow: local work.
